title: 🏛️ US Treasury Secretary: no new restrictions on Nvidia chips to China!
body: 🏛️ US Treasury Secretary: no new restrictions on Nvidia chips to China!

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said imposing additional restrictions to stop Nvidia exporting its older chips to China is "no longer necessary", after the US administration moved to block Chinese companies from remotely accessing advanced AI chips and servers.
Bessent added in a television interview after returning from an Asian tour with President Trump: "The appropriate chip restrictions are in place", and "remote access has been scaled back".

His remarks came a day after the House Foreign Affairs Committee published Commerce Department records revealing approval for the sale of 879,868 Nvidia and AMD AI chips to China-linked companies, out of more than 3.4 million chips requested, including 150,000 chips for Tencent, 75,000 for Alibaba, 43,000 for Baidu and 4,000 for BYD.

Nvidia said its limited shipments of H200 chips were legal and authorised, and that it had stopped shipping these chips to China despite earlier approvals, while AMD affirmed its commitment to US export-control laws.

In the same context, President Trump said he has "not lost confidence" in Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, despite controversy over the department's delay in imposing restrictions on Megaspeed, a company accused of diverting restricted Nvidia chips to China.

Simply put: after Congress revealed hundreds of thousands of chips approved for China, the US Treasury says the current restrictions are enough — and the new door China was entering through, remote access, has been closed.
Are the current restrictions enough to stop advanced chips reaching China, or will smuggling find another way?
